prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Rebuild Hokusai’s *Great Wave* as a gently animated low-poly wallpaper.

[action] Created [scene/index.html](<WORKSPACE>/scene/index.html) and [result.json](<WORKSPACE>/result.json). I chose a fixed orthographic view with a slight vertical crop on widescreen displays. The artwork is built in code and opens directly in a browser.

[result] I visually checked the original-ratio and widescreen renders. The browser requested only the specified Three.js module. The checks reported `Animation: screenshots differ across frames`, `Reduced motion: screenshots match across frames`, and `Browser process closed`.

[next] The print shows **three boats** and **Mount Fuji**. I counted the boats at left, middle right, and foreground in `print.jpg`. The Met’s catalog confirms the boat count and identifies Fuji in the hollow of the wave. [The Metropolitan Museum of Art](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/56353)
